base_properties.human_readable: Sex-Gender Category Membership by Identity Self-Identification

perspectives.label: Trans Women (Self-Identification Primary Beneficiaries)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: TRANS WOMEN (ROPE) — Genuine coordination benefit from identity-based category membership: legal recognition, access to gendered services and spaces, social intelligibility. Low suppression relative to exit capacity; mobile exit options (can organize, advocate, relocate). Experienced as coordination mechanism enabling social inclusion and legal recognition. Net beneficiary position with agency.

perspectives.label: Cis Women Advocating Sex-Based Protections
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: CIS WOMEN (SEX-BASED PROTECTION ADVOCACY) (TANGLED ROPE) — Experience mixed coordination and extraction. Benefit from the category system's legal and social coordination (sex-based protections, single-sex spaces). Simultaneously bear asymmetric extraction: lose exclusive claim to sex-based legal protections; must negotiate access and safety in previously single-sex spaces; face social/political pressure for exclusionary boundary maintenance. Constrained by moderate costs (social penalty, political friction) but not trapped — can organize, advocate, relocate.

perspectives.label: Single-Sex Space Users with Vulnerability
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: SINGLE-SEX SPACE USERS WITH VULNERABILITY (SNARE) — Trapped parties (incarcerated women, domestic violence survivors in shelters, survivors of male sexual violence seeking safe bathing/toileting spaces). Suppression is maximal: no exit options; cannot reorganize space access; bear full cost of boundary redefinition with minimal power to negotiate. Experience pure extraction — their spatial safety is traded against inclusionary boundary logic. Highest experienced extraction; zero degrees of freedom.

perspectives.label: Legal Institutions & Space-Providing Organizations
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: LEGAL & SPACE-PROVIDING INSTITUTIONS (TANGLED ROPE) — Govern category boundaries and space access. Benefit from clarified category definitions (reduces litigation, enables policy). Simultaneously extracted from: face conflicting legal mandates (anti-discrimination law vs sex-based protection law), high compliance costs, political pressure from multiple constituencies, liability exposure. Constrained but not trapped — can shift policy, negotiate boundaries, appeal to higher authority.

perspectives.label: Identity Rights Advocacy Coalition
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: IDENTITY RIGHTS ADVOCACY COALITION (SCAFFOLD) — Organized advocates (LGBTQ+ organizations, trans rights groups) see self-identification as a temporary bridge toward deeper institutional redesign: replacing sex-based categories with identity-based ones in law and policy. Experience the constraint as soluble — enforcement through legal recognition, institutional policy change, and norm shift. Have organized power and exit visibility; see sunset in category dissolution itself rather than in the identity rule. Theater is moderate (some performative inclusion without functional boundary resolution).

perspectives.label: Historical Sex-Classification Institutional Apparatus
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: HISTORICAL SEX-CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (PITON) — The traditional biological sex classification system (chromosomes, anatomy, reproductive capacity) persists institutionally through inertia despite its legitimacy being substantially challenged. Medical systems, legal systems, and data infrastructure continue to collect and enforce sex categories not because they function for their original purpose but because the infrastructure is expensive to replace. Theater ratio is high (the biological categories are maintained ceremonially while real social power is increasingly organized around identity). The apparatus has degraded function but institutional persistence.

perspectives.label: Natural Law View (Immutable Biology)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 7: NATURAL LAW / IMMUTABILITY VIEW (MOUNTAIN) — Some perspectives claim that sex category membership is a natural law: biological reproduction has two poles; organisms are reliably classifiable as male or female; this classification is immutable and pre-social. From this view, self-identification cannot change material category membership; boundary maintenance is costless. However, this perspective is a false-summit candidate: identifiable institutional beneficiaries maintain this naturalization (traditional sex-based protections industries, biological taxonomy enforcement structures), and the constraint is better modeled as a constructed system than as natural law.

perspectives.label: Analytical Observer (Institutional Decomposition)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 8: ANALYTICAL OBSERVER (TANGLED ROPE) — Sees the sex-gender category system as a constructed institutional apparatus with genuine coordination functions (legal rights, medical treatment, statistical reporting) and asymmetric extraction (boundary enforcement burdens, exclusion from categories, space contestation). The identity reading is one reconstruction of this apparatus among others; its extractiveness depends on how thoroughly alternative boundaries are enforced and who bears the costs of ambiguity and transition.

omegas.question: Does the identity reading's foundational premise (identity determines category membership) logically foreclose the biology reading's core premise (immutable biology determines membership), or do they coexist as competing live options?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Logical analysis: Can both axioms be held simultaneously in a single coherent framework? Identity-determined membership does not deny that biological properties exist, but it denies that biological properties *determine* category membership. Biology reading denies that identity alone is sufficient. Either (a) both premises coexist as competing readings within different institutional frameworks (coexists_with), or (b) the identity reading forecloses biology only if it claims identity OVERRIDES biological facts entirely (rare — most identity readings grant biological facts but deny categorization follows automatically).
omegas.impact: If forecloses: identity reading and biology reading cannot both be law in any single jurisdiction. If coexists_with: multiple frameworks can coexist (some institutions use identity, others use biology). If influences: identity reading shifts resource allocation and legitimacy but does not logically rule out biology reading.
omegas.description: Whether identity reading logically rules out biology reading or both coexist as live options

omegas.question: Who bears the primary enforcement cost when identity-determined category membership conflicts with single-sex space access policies — the individuals seeking access, the space-providing institution, or the existing users?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Empirical analysis of actual policy implementations: track who incurs costs (institutional liability, individual delay, exclusion from space, contested access). Cost allocation determines whether the constraint is experienced as tangled rope (shared burden) or snare (burden concentrated on powerless).
omegas.impact: If institutions bear enforcement cost: tangled rope from institutional perspective (constrained but not trapped). If vulnerable space users bear cost (exclusion, access delay, safety compromise): snare from their perspective (trapped, maximal extraction). If individuals seeking access bear cost (documentation requirements, institutional delay, social friction): constrains their exit options, shifts their classification upward (trapped → constrained).
omegas.description: Who bears primary enforcement cost for identity-based category access

omegas.question: Is the long-term trajectory of this identity reading toward elimination of sex-gender categories altogether, or toward dualization (separate identity-based and biology-based categories coexisting)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Examine advocacy coalition goals and institutional implementation patterns over 10-year window. Dualization (two parallel category systems) produces different extraction dynamics than dissolution (collapsing categories entirely).
omegas.impact: If trajectory is dissolution: the identity reading is a scaffold toward category elimination — theater is high in the transition, but suppression would fall to zero when categories dissolve. If trajectory is dualization: tangled rope persists indefinitely — two category systems create new conflicts and enforcement costs. If trajectory is identity replacement (identity categories fully replace biology): similar to dissolution but with different institutional history.
omegas.description: Long-term institutional trajectory — category dissolution, dualization, or identity replacement

omegas.question: In this identity reading, are trans women primarily beneficiaries (gain category access and legal recognition) or primarily victims (face social suppression, institutional gatekeeping, violence)? Is the classification stable or does it shift by context?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Structural analysis: Beneficiary status derives from gaining access to identity-congruent category and associated legal protections. Victim status derives from facing suppression (violence, institutional denial, social exclusion) when the identity reading is NOT yet institutionalized. In jurisdictions where identity-based category membership is law and enforced: trans women are beneficiaries. In jurisdictions where identity reading is contested or resisted: trans women bear costs of the struggle (suppression) and are partially victims. The reading instantiates both roles depending on institutional implementation.
omegas.impact: If trans women are net beneficiaries (institutional implementation secure): perspectives shift toward rope/scaffold. If trans women remain targets of suppression despite formal category membership: snare/tangled_rope perspectives persist. The constraint's extractiveness is higher when the identity reading is contested law (suppression is high) than when it is secure law (suppression is low but enforcement costs shift to cis women).
omegas.description: Whether trans women experience primarily beneficiary or victim role, and how this shifts by jurisdiction and time

omegas.question: Does the identity reading itself (as a logical/ontological claim about what determines category membership) differ structurally from the institutional enforcement of that reading (policies, regulations, procedures)? Are they the same constraint or two related constraints?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Decomposition analysis: The reading (ontological claim: identity determines membership) is an abstract commitment. The enforcement (institutional policies, penalties, access procedures) is a mechanism. They have different ε values: the reading itself has low base extractiveness (it is simply a claim); the enforcement apparatus has higher extractiveness (it regulates behavior and allocates costs). Should decompose into two linked constraints: one story about the reading as commitment system, one about the enforcement apparatus.
omegas.impact: If they are the same constraint: ε is conflated across logical and institutional levels. If they are separate constraints: the reading has lower ε (it is contestable ontology); the enforcement has higher ε (it is institutional apparatus with costs). The schema currently treats them as one (the identity reading as instantiated in this story) — this omega documents the decomposition possibility for future authoring.
omegas.description: Whether the identity reading (ontological claim) and its institutional enforcement (policy/regulatory apparatus) are one constraint or two

omegas.question: What is the current empirical and institutional status of the sibling readings (biology_reading, hybrid_reading) relative to this identity reading? Do they represent live legal alternatives, superseded positions, or coexisting frameworks?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Jurisdictional inventory: Which readings are enacted into law, which are advocated as alternatives, which are treated as superseded or foreclosed? Temporal analysis: Are readings shifting (biology toward piton status, identity toward normalization), stable, or cyclical?
omegas.impact: If biology reading is coexisting law (some jurisdictions use identity, others use biology): classification is coexists_with, and the constraint's extractiveness varies by jurisdiction. If biology reading is treated as foreclosed (actively rejected): influences or forecloses relation. If biology reading is piton status (persists through inertia despite being de-legitimized): institutional persistence affects measurements.
omegas.description: Current institutional and legal status of biology and hybrid readings relative to identity reading

commentary.narrative_context: This constraint describes sex-gender category membership determined by subjective identity self-identification — the claim that an individual's gender category (woman, man, etc.) is determined by their stated gender identity rather than by biological properties, reproductive anatomy, chromosomes, or medical gatekeeping. This is ONE READING of a contested kernel. The same social practice — categorizing individuals by gender — is read differently across three competing institutional frameworks: (1) biology_reading: category membership determined by immutable reproductive biology; (2) hybrid_reading: membership determined by combination of biology and social transition (medical/legal gatekeeping); (3) identity_reading: membership determined by subjective identity alone (the reading instantiated in this constraint story). Each reading reconstructs the category system with different beneficiaries, victims, and enforcement costs. The identity reading produces a tangled rope from most perspectives because it genuinely coordinates social recognition and legal access for trans women while simultaneously extracting from cis women (loss of exclusive claim to sex-based protections) and from certain vulnerable populations (single-sex space users who need exclusive access for safety). The suppression metrics show accumulation over the interval: as the identity reading gains institutional traction (policies, legal recognition, norm shifts), the suppression requirement increases — enforcement must overcome the resistance from institutions built on alternative readings. The theater ratio reflects that significant performative activity surrounds identity verification (administrative procedures, institutional policies, social negotiation) without fully resolving the underlying access conflicts.
key_agents: Trans women: Primary beneficiaries (moderate/mobile) — gain legal and social recognition of gender identity; access gendered services and spaces; achieve institutional intelligibility
Cis women advocating sex-based protections: Asymmetric losers (moderate/constrained) — lose exclusive claim to sex-based legal protections; must negotiate shared space access; face political pressure

Single-sex space users with vulnerability: Trapped victims (powerless/trapped) — incarcerated women, survivors in shelters, abuse survivors seeking safety in single-sex spaces; face exclusion or contested access

Legal institutions and space-providing organizations: Conflicted regulators (institutional/constrained) — govern category boundaries; face conflicting legal mandates; bear compliance and liability costs

Identity rights advocacy coalition: Organized beneficiaries (organized/constrained) — trans rights organizations, LGBTQ+ advocates; see identity reading as solving a classification injustice; have organizing power
Biology-reading traditionalists: Displaced defenders (various power levels/constrained) — resist identity reading as ontologically incoherent; advocate for biological category preservation

Hybrid-reading gatekeepers: Alternative-pathway administrators (institutional/constrained) — medical, legal, and social systems maintaining medical/legal transition requirements; see themselves displaced by identity reading
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.52): Moderate-high. The identity reading produces genuine benefits (legal recognition, access, inclusion) alongside genuine harms (loss of exclusive sex-based protections, space contestation, enforcement costs). The asymmetry is real and measurable, but the coordination function (establishing who belongs in which social/legal categories) is not purely extractive. Suppression (0.68): Moderately high and rising. Rising because institutional entrenchment of alternative readings (biology, hybrid) creates resistance to identity-based reclassification; enforcement requires overcoming legal, institutional, and social opposition. Theater ratio (0.55): Moderate. Identity verification procedures (how institutions actually determine category membership claims) involve substantial performative elements (documentation requirements, administrative review, social negotiation) without fully resolving boundary ambiguity. Claimed type (Tangled Rope): The constraint has genuine coordination function (establishing inclusive categories, enabling legal recognition, providing social intelligibility) AND asymmetric extraction (cis women lose exclusive protections, vulnerable space users lose safe-access guarantee). Both elements are present; the constraint cannot be reduced to pure extraction (snare) because the coordination benefit is real, nor to pure coordination (rope) because the extraction burden is substantial and concentrated on identifiable groups.
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality varies dramatically by agent structural position. Trans women (beneficiaries with mobile exit options and moderate power) derive low directionality d (toward 0.0), producing negative χ — the constraint subsidizes their position. Cis women advocating sex-based protections (victims with constrained exit and moderate power) derive higher d (toward 0.60–0.70), producing moderate-high χ. Single-sex space users with vulnerability (victims with trapped exit and powerless position) derive maximal d (toward 0.95), producing maximum χ — the constraint extracts from them at the highest possible rate. Institutional actors (regulated space-providers) derive d in the 0.50–0.65 range depending on whether they benefit from institutional clarity (law favoring their preferred reading) or are extracted from (law requiring costly accommodation). The analytical observer derives d around 0.72 (observer position), showing moderate-high experienced extractiveness because the observer sees all sides' costs and benefits without beneficiary status.
commentary.perspectival_gap: Extraordinary. The same constraint classifies as rope (trans women beneficiaries), tangled rope (cis women paying mixed costs), snare (vulnerable space users trapped), scaffold (advocates seeing sunset in category dissolution), piton (traditional sex-classification apparatus persisting through inertia), and mountain (naturalization of biology). The gap reveals not measurement error but fundamental disagreement about what the constraint IS — not just disagreement about whether it is good. Trans women's perspective: 'This is a classification that includes me and coordinates my access.' Cis women's perspective: 'This is a system that redistributes who gets sex-based protections.' Vulnerable space users' perspective: 'This is a rule that takes away my access to safe space.' Advocates' perspective: 'This is a temporary bridge toward category reform.' Institutional perspective: 'This is a conflicting mandate I must enforce.' The naturalization perspective: 'This violates the facts of biology itself.' None of these is 'wrong' — they are all true from their structural position. The perspectival gap is the constraint's signature.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: READING-SPECIFIC MANDATROPHY: The identity reading resolves mandatrophy not by being one 'correct' type but by showing that mandatrophy itself is an artifact of trying to classify a contested reading as a single institution type. The reading IS tangled rope: it coordinates category membership (genuine function) alongside extraction (asymmetric burden). Both are structural. The reading is also snare from the perspective of those who lose exclusive space access. It is also rope from the perspective of trans women gaining recognition. It is also piton from the perspective of the traditional sex-classification system that no longer functions but persists. The identity reading's mandatrophy is not 'coordination or extraction?' but 'whose framework determines the answer?' Because this is a kernel reading — a contested commitment system — the answer depends on which authority structure adjudicates the classification. In jurisdictions adopting the identity reading into law, the mandatrophy resolves toward tangled rope (balancing recognition and burden). In jurisdictions maintaining the biology reading, the mandatrophy resolves toward snare or piton (traditional system persisting). The reading does not have a single mandatrophy resolution — it instantiates different resolutions in different institutional contexts.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint is ONE READING of the contested kernel 'sex-gender category membership.' The kernel is: what determines whether an individual belongs to the category 'woman' (or 'man' or other gender category)? The identity reading's answer: subjective identity self-identification. The biology reading's answer: immutable reproductive biology (chromosomes, anatomy, reproductive capacity). The hybrid reading's answer: combination of biology and social/medical transition. These are not different measurements of the same underlying fact — they are competing framings of what the social category MEANS. The identity reading forecloses the pure biology reading ONLY if it claims that identity overwrites biological facts entirely (rare). Most identity readings coexist with biology readings: 'Biological sex is a fact; but category membership is determined by identity.' This preserves biological truth while denying that biology determines classification. The hybrid reading is influenced by the identity reading: once identity claims institutional traction, the medical gatekeeping requirement becomes optional (you don't need medical transition to be recognized). The sibling readings coexist as live positions within different institutional frameworks. Some jurisdictions adopt the identity reading (legal category membership by identity alone). Others maintain the biology reading (category membership by chromosomes/anatomy). Others use hybrid (identity plus medical documentation). The readings do not coexist within a single legal framework — they divide the institutional landscape.

network.dual_formulation_note: The sex-gender category kernel has three constraint stories, one per reading. Each reading instantiates a different constraint with different ε values, beneficiary/victim sets, and institutional trajectories. This story (identity_reading) has ε=0.52 (tangled rope). The biology_reading has lower ε in jurisdictions where it is secure law but higher ε in jurisdictions where it is contested/piton status. The hybrid_reading has intermediate ε. All three are linked via network.affects_constraints because they are competing instantiations of a single kernel — changing which reading becomes law affects the others' extractiveness and classification. Upstream: single_sex_space_access_rights (the practical implementation of any reading) and sex_based_legal_protections (which reading affects protection allocation) both depend on which category reading is in force.
